messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Seabright (Private VPC) customer-facing API 503 spike

incident-bot: Details: CloudWatch alarm 'seabright-prod-5xx-rate' triggered at 2026-06-14T08:12:01Z. 5xx rate 31% over last 5m. Affected route: /api/v1/workflows. Sources: private VPC (seabright-prod). Pager sent to #incidents and oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I'm oncall, taking lead. ETA on triage 2m. Assigning roles: me (IC), ming (network), alex (app), rachel (customer comms).

oncall-sre: quick smoke: `curl -v https://seabright-api.internal/api/v1/health` ->
```
* TCP connection to 10.10.23.45 port 443 succeeded
> GET /api/v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: seabright-api.internal
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< content-type: application/json
{"status":"degraded","details":"downstream auth 503"}
```

customer-sre-seabright: We started seeing errors at ~08:10 UTC, yes. Customers report transaction failures. We can accept temporary network egress to partner auth service IP if needed.

ming: pulling target health from NLB target group:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/abcd1234
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id":"i-0aaa111"}, "TargetHealth": {"State":"unhealthy","Description":"Connection timed out"}},
    {"Target": {"Id":"i-0bbb222"}, "TargetHealth": {"State":"unhealthy","Description":"503 from backend"}}
  ]
}
```
Looks like targets failing healthcheck because backend returns 503 when contacting downstream auth.

alex: any recent deploys? I see a minimal app rollback at 07:58, nothing touching health endpoint. Checking pod logs (app runs inside private VPC instances):
```
2026-06-14T08:11:48Z error downstream auth call failed: connect ETIMEDOUT 54.23.11.77:443
2026-06-14T08:11:48Z warn healthcheck returning degraded
```

netops: I see a security group change merged 06/14 07:55 (PR #3421) that tightened egress to only allow outbound 443 to internal subnets — it removed a customer-allowed external IP range used for the partner auth. That would cause downstream calls to fail.

oncall-sre: ok probable root cause = SG egress tighten. Two mitigation paths: 1) add temporary egress rule to allow partner auth IP range 54.23.11.0/24; 2) change app healthcheck to not call external auth (short term) + rollback SG change PR. Which is fastest?

customer-sre-seabright: We approve option 1 (whitelist). Our compliance team ok with temporary allow and we'll revoke when done. Please test first in staging.

ming: preparing to apply temporary rule via AWS console/CLI. Will run `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 54.23.11.0/24 --description 'temp allow partner auth for incident 1769554321'`

oncall-sre: please add the exact command you're about to run in thread and request approval from netops for terraform drift.

ming: running now, netops please ack.

netops: ack. also open PR to revert SG change and mark as emergency revert — we're good with temporary CLI change but create terraform PR to avoid drift.

ming: (2m later) CLI applied. New egress rule id: ega-0f1e2d3c. Verifying app:
```
curl -v https://seabright-api.internal/api/v1/health
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok"}
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: CloudWatch alarm cleared at 2026-06-14T08:20:02Z. 5xx rate down to 0.8% over last 5m.

rachel: customer notified: "we just fixed an infrastructure change that impacted connectivity to an external auth provider; temporary firewall rule added; will revert after review". Customer asked for ETA on revert.

oncall-sre: follow-ups: (1) netops to open terraform PR to revert PR#3421 or re-add proper egress in IaC, (2) app team to add better local-only health endpoint (no external calls) for the next release, (3) run canary for 30m, (4) schedule postmortem. I'll create the incident ticket and add action owners.

netops: PR opened -> https://git.example.com/netops/infra/merge_requests/789. Marking as urgent revert, pipeline queued. We'll coordinate with customer for maintenance window to finalize.

customer-sre-seabright: thanks, scope looks good. We'll expect revert in 24h, okay to keep temp rule until then.

oncall-sre: handing off to follow-up owner ming for monitoring. I'm signing out but will join postmortem. :handshake:

ming: taking follow-up. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then hand to morning rotation. :eyes:

alex: ending note: postmortem should include test coverage for SG changes and gate for outbound egress removal when services have external dependencies.

rachel: adding severity to ticket P1 -> incident-1769554321. Logged customer impact and communications. :notebook:

oncall-sre: incident resolved. Closing thread once PR merges and temp rule removed. :white_check_mark:
